title: Types of angles
keyIdea: An angle measures turn: how far one arm has turned from the other around the vertex. A quarter turn is a right angle (90°), marked with a small square. Acute angles are smaller than 90°, obtuse angles are between 90° and 180°, a straight line is 180° and reflex angles are more than 180°. The length of the arms does not change the angle. Diagrams use marks so you can read facts without measuring: matching ticks mean equal sides, matching arcs mean equal angles, and in ∠ABC the middle letter, B, is the vertex.

kid: Stand up and face the door. Turn until you face the side wall. That quarter turn is a right angle. It is 90°. On a drawing it gets a small square in the corner. Two right angles make a half turn, a straight line of 180°. Four make a full turn of 360°.

Angles have names. Smaller than a right angle is acute. Between a right angle and a straight line is obtuse. More than a straight line is reflex. Turning the page does not change the type. A tilted right angle is still a right angle.
The size of an angle is the turn, not the length of the arms. If you draw longer arms on the same angle, the opening stays the same. Do not let long arms fool you.

Maths drawings use marks. Sides with the same number of ticks are the same length. Angles with the same arc are equal. In ∠ABC the angle is at B, the middle letter. Use the marks to find missing angles: on a straight line the angles add up to 180°.
adult: This lesson follows the English national curriculum for Years 3 to 6. In Year 3 pupils 'recognise angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn', 'identify right angles, recognise that two right angles make a half-turn, three make three quarters of a turn and four a complete turn', and 'identify whether angles are greater than or less than a right angle'. In Year 4 they 'identify acute and obtuse angles and compare and order angles up to two right angles by size'. In Year 6 they find missing angles. US Common Core 4.MD.5 to 4.MD.7 treat angle measure as turn in degrees and as additive.

The diagram conventions are standard. A small square marks a right angle. Single or double ticks show sides of equal length. Matching arcs show equal angles. An angle is named with three letters such as ∠ABC (the vertex is always the middle letter) or with a single letter or number. Facts that come from these marks, such as angles on a straight line adding to 180° and angles round a point adding to 360°, let pupils find unknown angles without a protractor.

Common mistakes to watch for: thinking that longer arms or a bigger drawn arc make a bigger angle; only recognising a right angle when one arm is horizontal; reading a tick as 1 cm or as a parallel mark (parallel lines use arrows); naming ∠ABC as the angle at A; and using 360° for angles on a straight line. Ask 'how far has it turned?' rather than 'how big does it look?', and turn the page to show that orientation does not matter.

In the lab you turn an arm to make one, two and three right angles, sort tilted and reflex angles by type, compare angles with arms of different lengths, read the marks on an isosceles triangle, and use the marks to find a missing angle on a straight line, inside a right angle and round a point.

familyTip: Make a right-angle checker by folding a scrap of paper in half and then in half again. Hunt round the house together for corners that are right angles, smaller (acute) or bigger (obtuse). Then open a door or a laptop slowly and call out each type as the angle grows.

visual.caption: What type of angle is it? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: turn an arm, sort angles by type, test longer arms, read diagram marks and find missing angles.

practice.prompt: Two angles sit on a straight line. One is {a}°. How many degrees is the other angle, x?
practice.hint: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Take {a} away from 180.

practice.prompt: A right angle, marked with a small square, is split into two parts. One part is {a}°. How big is the other part?
practice.hint: The small square means the whole corner is 90°. Subtract the part you know.
practice.explain: 90 − {a} = {=90-a}, so the other part is {=90-a}°. Both parts together make the right angle.

practice.prompt: An angle is 135°. What type of angle is it?
practice.hint: Is it more than a right angle (90°)? Is it less than a straight line (180°)?
practice.explain: 135° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse. Acute is under 90° and reflex is over 180°.

practice.prompt: In a diagram, sides PQ and RS each have two tick marks. What does that tell you?
choices: PQ and RS are each 2 cm
PQ and RS are the same length
practice.hint: Ticks do not give a length. They pair up sides with the same number of marks.
practice.explain: Matching tick marks mean equal lengths, so PQ = RS. Parallel lines are shown with arrows, not ticks.

pool.prompt: Three angles meet at a point. Two of them are {a}° and {b}°. What is the third angle?
pool.hint: Angles round a point make a full turn, 360°. Take away both angles you know.

pool.prompt: A clock hand turns through {n} right angles. How many degrees is that?
pool.hint: Each right angle is a quarter turn, which is 90°.
pool.explain: {n} × 90 = {=n*90}, so the hand turns {=n*90}°. Four right angles would be a full turn of 360°.

pool.prompt: Angle P is 50° with arms 2 cm long. Angle Q is 50° with arms 8 cm long. Which is bigger?
pool.hint: An angle measures the turn between the arms, not how long they are.
pool.explain: Both turn through 50°, so they are the same size. Longer arms do not make a bigger angle.

pool.prompt: In triangle ABC, which angle is ∠BCA?
pool.hint: With three letters, the vertex of the angle is always the middle letter.
pool.explain: The middle letter of ∠BCA is C, so it is the angle at C, between sides CB and CA.

pool.prompt: A right angle is drawn tilted, so neither arm is flat. What type of angle is it?
pool.hint: Turning the whole angle round does not change how far one arm is from the other.
pool.explain: It is still 90°, a right angle. The direction an angle faces does not change its type.

pool.prompt: Ravi says two angles on a straight line are 100° and 260°. What went wrong?
pool.hint: A straight line is a half turn. How many degrees is a half turn?
pool.explain: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so the other angle is 80°. He used the full turn, 360°.

pool.prompt: Two angles in a triangle have the same arc mark. One is 40°. What do you know about the other?
pool.hint: Matching arcs tell you which angles are equal, just as ticks do for sides.
pool.explain: Matching arcs mean equal angles, so the other one is also 40°. No measuring is needed.

pool.prompt: Which of these is a reflex angle?
pool.hint: A reflex angle is more than a straight line, which is 180°.
pool.explain: 210° is more than 180°, so it is reflex. 175° is obtuse and 90° is a right angle.
